clue.text: Gestures 'owzat!', perhaps while stifling quiet and loud sound

indicators.note: to stifle is to smother, so the outer word closes around what it muffles

parts.note: as in 'as he spoke' means while he spoke
p, piano, is the musical mark for quiet
a peal is a loud ringing sound, as of bells or thunder

explanation.surface: A cricketer shouts 'Howzat!' to the umpire while muffling some noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Owzat (how's that?) is the cry fielders make in cricket to ask the umpire to give a batsman out.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket the fielding side's shout of 'owzat' is formally called an appeal, so a side doing it is said to make appeals.

clue.text: Silvery metal briefly offered by gutted Poirot

parts.words: Silvery metal briefly offered by gutted Poirot
parts.note: surface reading: a detective handing over a shiny piece of metal
setter's reading: Poirot with its insides removed leaves P and T, the chemical symbol, i.e. the brief form, of the metal wanted

explanation.surface: A deflated Hercule Poirot hands over a shiny piece of silvery metal.
explanation.walkthrough: Strip Poirot of its middle and PT is left; Pt is the chemical symbol of PLATINUM, so the metal is 'briefly' offered by the emptied name.
explanation.definitionFit: Platinum is a dense, precious, greyish-white element, which is why its colour gives the word for silvery blonde hair.

clue.text: Not casual, order starters from Avon Ladies

parts.note: form can mean order or arrangement, as in 'in good form'

indicators.note: starters are the opening letters, so only the first letter of each following word is taken

parts.note: the first letters of Avon and Ladies

explanation.surface: An instruction to dress smartly when you put in an order with Avon cosmetics sellers.
explanation.walkthrough: Avon Ladies are door-to-door sellers of Avon cosmetics, a familiar British sight.
explanation.definitionFit: Formal is the opposite of casual, describing dress or manner that follows convention.

clue.text: Old pears, say, might feed this fitful yachter on vacation at sea

definitions.text: Old pears, say, might feed this

indicators.note: something at sea is all over the place, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a word on vacation is emptied of its middle, so only its outside letters remain

parts.note: the first and last letters of yachter

explanation.surface: A queasy yachtsman, sick at sea, might be fed rotten pears.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruit flies lay their eggs in rotting or overripe fruit, so old pears are a food source for this insect.

clue.text: Neat in Ireland on the right-hand side

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a small breed of cattle originating in Ireland; neat is an old word for cattle
second meaning: the heraldic and Latin-derived word for right

explanation.walkthrough: 'Neat' looks like tidy or undiluted, as of whiskey in an Irish bar, but it is the old word for cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: Dexter is both the name of a small Irish cattle breed and the heraldic term for the right side of a shield.

clue.text: Spendthrift lived in olden days on bottom of barrel

parts.note: wast is the archaic second-person past form of be, as in 'thou wast'

indicators.note: only the lower end of the word is wanted, so its top part is dropped

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A spendthrift who once lived well is now at the bottom of the barrel.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the BAR from barrel to leave its bottom part, REL. 'Lived' stands for 'existed', which old English writes as wast.
explanation.definitionFit: A wastrel is a good-for-nothing who squanders money, so a spendthrift is a fair synonym.

clue.text: Sun god's head between two levels?

indicators.note: something between two things sits in the gap, with one on each side

parts.note: A-level and O-level, two grades of British school exam
poll is an old word for the head

explanation.surface: A question about where the sun god's head sits, as if between two storeys.
explanation.walkthrough: A-levels and O-levels are British school exams, once taken at 18 and 16.
explanation.definitionFit: Apollo was the Greek and Roman god associated with the sun, light and music.

clue.text: Unruly man with spare cheese

indicators.note: unruly things refuse to stay in line, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An unruly man is carrying a spare chunk of cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Parmesan is a hard Italian cheese, often grated over pasta.

clue.text: Errant idiocy, all about husband supporting bar's time off?

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting part sits underneath, so it follows the other piece

parts.note: a pub is a bar

indicators.note: about means going round, so the jumbled letters wrap the single letter
errant means straying, so the letters wander out of order

parts.note: taken as written
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A grumble about idiotic carry-on, with the husband propping up the bar on his day off.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of IDIOCY ALL with H inside sits below PUB. The question mark flags that 'time off' is a loose description.
explanation.definitionFit: A public holiday is a day when most people are given a break from work, such as a bank holiday.

clue.text: Rebellious lot blunder when occupied by rug's backing

indicators.note: backing means moving in reverse, so the combined letters are read from the end
something occupied has another thing living inside it

parts.note: a boner is a silly mistake
a mat is a small rug

explanation.surface: A rebellious crowd blunders when it occupies the space behind a rug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rug's backing' reads as the underside of a carpet, but backing works on the whole of BO(MAT)NER.
explanation.definitionFit: A rent-a-mob is a crowd hired or easily assembled to protest, so a rebellious lot.

clue.text: Fully enthusiastic about skin of tomato

parts.note: to be into something is to be keen on it

indicators.note: the skin is the outer layer, so only the outside letters of the word are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of tomato

explanation.surface: Someone wholly keen on the peel of a tomato.
explanation.definitionFit: In toto is Latin for 'in total', meaning completely or entirely.

clue.text: Avenue on lake, bad round Welsh town

indicators.note: in an across clue one thing on another follows it, so the lake comes first

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for lake
a lane is a road or avenue

indicators.note: turned round means facing the other way, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: ill means bad, as in ill will

explanation.surface: A trip round a Welsh town where the avenue by the lake is in a bad state.
explanation.definitionFit: Llanelli is a town in Carmarthenshire, south Wales, known for its rugby club.

clue.text: Cut from memory, fabricate temperature

parts.note: to forge is to fabricate or fake
T is the abbreviation for temperature

explanation.surface: Advice to delete something from memory and make up the temperature reading instead.
explanation.definitionFit: To forget something is to lose it from your memory, as if snipped out.

clue.text: Eastern poet ahoy dancing around record one month back

indicators.note: around means encircling, so the reshuffled letters go round the next piece
dancing letters move about, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
a mark is a recorded score

indicators.note: going back means returning the way it came, so the word reads in reverse

parts.note: May is one month of the year

explanation.surface: A sailor's cry, 'Ahoy!', set to dance music on a record made a month ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Record' as a noun suggests a disc, but here it is a score or tally; the shuffled letters split to sit either side of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Omar Khayyam was the medieval Persian poet of the Rubaiyat, and Persia lies to the east of Europe.

clue.text: Niece for one on the subject of zip in tongue

parts.note: re means concerning or on the subject of

indicators.note: one thing in another is placed inside it

parts.note: a tongue is a language, and Latin is one
zip means zero, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A niece talks on a subject with a zip through her tongue piercing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Zip' is American slang for zero, which crosswords read as O.
explanation.definitionFit: A niece is one example of a family member, a relation by blood or marriage.

clue.text: Sound in mind, parcel out with present has nothing going astray

indicators.note: the zero-shaped letter wanders off, so it is dropped from the first piece

parts.note: to allot is to parcel out or share
here means present, as in a roll call

explanation.surface: A sound-minded person shares out a parcel and the gift goes missing.
explanation.walkthrough: Nothing is the letter O, zero's lookalike.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is all there is mentally alert and fully in possession of their wits, an idiom for sane.

clue.text: Impugning small child (not half) in prison (not half)

indicators.note: one thing in another is set inside it
not half means half the word is thrown away, leaving its first half

parts.note: Sing Sing is a famous prison in New York State
a nipper is a small child

explanation.surface: Accusing a small child of being half in prison.
explanation.walkthrough: Sing Sing is a famous New York State prison, and a nipper is British slang for a small child; each loses its second half.
explanation.definitionFit: Sniping means making sly critical attacks, much as impugning calls someone's honesty into question.

clue.text: Continue to live in Haiti with exhausted Bermudan flies

indicators.note: letters that fly about land in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: exhausted means emptied out, so only the outside letters remain

parts.note: the first and last letters of Bermudan

explanation.surface: A worn-out Bermudan stays on in Haiti, swatting flies.
explanation.definitionFit: To inhabit a place is to dwell in it, so to keep living in a home.

clue.text: Ready to work some shellac novelty boomerangs

indicators.note: a boomerang flies back the way it came, so the letters run in reverse
some means only a part, so the letters lie inside the phrase

parts.note: the run inside shELLAC NOvelty

explanation.surface: A novelty shellac boomerang is ready for use.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor on call is available to be summoned to work at short notice.

clue.text: Adult cat maybe in charge of a bomb?

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for adult, as in film ratings
a tom is a male cat
IC is the abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: Is a grown-up cat in command of a bomb?
explanation.definitionFit: Atomic describes the kind of bomb that releases energy by nuclear fission, as dropped on Hiroshima.

clue.text: Enter claw in shelter for much less

indicators.note: to enter is to go inside, so one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: the lee is the sheltered side
a talon is a bird's claw

explanation.surface: A bird of prey's claw reaches into a shelter, and much less is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Let alone is an idiom used like 'never mind' or 'much less': he can't walk, let alone run.

clue.text: Last of goulash eaten by testy, angry sea goddess

indicators.note: something eaten by another ends up inside it
angry means worked up, so the letters are stirred around

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter

parts.note: the final letter of goulash

explanation.surface: A testy, angry sea goddess eats the end of a goulash.
explanation.definitionFit: Tethys was a Titaness of Greek myth, a goddess of the sea and wife of Oceanus.

clue.text: Away pursuing odd characters in superb shoot

indicators.note: pursuing means following behind, so this piece comes second
the odd characters are those in first, third and fifth place

parts.note: the 1st, 3rd and 5th letters of superb
out means away, as in 'she is out'

explanation.surface: Away on a superb shoot, chasing odd characters.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprout is a new shoot growing from a plant.

clue.text: DNA, much altered, limiting tense European

indicators.note: limiting means hemming in, so the jumble surrounds a letter
altered letters are changed in order

parts.note: taken as written
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A tense European whose DNA has been heavily altered.
explanation.definitionFit: A Dutchman is a man from the Netherlands, so a European.

clue.text: Individual who's misanthropic in no matter which element

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it

parts.note: any means no matter which, as in 'pick any card'
Timon of Athens, Shakespeare's hater of mankind

explanation.surface: A misanthrope sits inside some element or other.
explanation.definitionFit: Antimony is a chemical element, a brittle metalloid with the symbol Sb.

clue.text: Northern city regularly sized small dog

parts.note: York is a city in the north of England

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken

parts.note: the 2nd and 4th letters of sized

explanation.surface: A northern city's dog, regularly sized up as small.
explanation.definitionFit: Yorkie is the familiar short name for a Yorkshire terrier, a toy breed of dog.
